newsitem.title: USA: Stocks sharply higher, bonds lend a hand.
newsitem.headline: Stocks sharply higher, bonds lend a hand.

text.p: Wall Street stocks rose on Friday, boosted by a rallying bond market and a steady stream of solid corporate earnings reports.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow was up 64.46 points at 7,951.22.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 16-9 on heavy volume of 295 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 9.51 points to 1,500.44.

The long bond gave the stock market much of its upward drive, analysts said. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rallied 13/32 to a 6.53 percent yield, down from Thursday's yield of 6.56 percent after the June Producer Price Index data showed scant evidence of inflation.

"The bond market is the no brainer here today," said Doug Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at J.P. Morgan. "The bond market has really been the key to the equity market since Memorial Day weekend, and they have been moving in tandem."
Even though the stock market has reached such high valuations, it used an extra boost from a strong bond market and a lower interest rate outlook to rise further, Cliggott said.

"It's a combination of the bond market providing interest rate direction and the kind of earnings which come out, offering an outlook on the third quarter and the remainder of the year," said Sam Stovall, an analyst at S&P Industry Reports.

Financial markets got a lift after the Labour Department reported that the June Producer Price Index, forecast to be unchanged, fell 0.1 percent. The core PPI, excluding the food and energy components, rose 0.1 percent, as estimated.
Wholesale prices declined for a record sixth straight month during June, the government said.

"Everybody was waiting for those numbers this morning, and when the PPI showed no surprises, it bolstered the bond market, which tooks stocks with it," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.

A good earnings outlook for the technology sector helped that sector and the broader stock market, he said. "Technology is helping to lead the way up. There have been very few negative earnings surprises."
Intel Corp. gained 1-1/8 to 151-1/4, while Compaq Computer Corp. rose 2-15/16 to 123-1/4. Hewlett-Packard Co. rose 2-6/16 to 60-11/16 and Atmel Corp. added 2-7/8 to 31-3/8.
Atmel posted second-quarter earnings of 27 cents per share, compared with 50 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. Alex Brown said it upgraded the shares to buy from market perform.

Among other issues, MCI Communications Corp. sank 6-3/16 to 36-3/16, after the telecommunications company said it expected earnings for the second half of 1997 and going into 1998 to be below Wall Street expectations.
